ai.title: Prompt tuning for file reading and plan execution
ai.summary: Updated system prompts to enforce aggressive file reading before edits and mandate complete plan implementation. Replaced 'think_deeply' references with 'create_plan' in agent instructions. Modified `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` and `backend/src/system-prompt/agent-instructions.md` to prioritize context acquisition and full task execution over minimal steps.

eli5.text: The assistant you interact with has been given clearer instructions about how to approach your requests. Instead of rushing to make minimal changes, it is now told to read more files first and then carry out your full plan rather than stopping halfway. If you give it a multi-step task, you'll notice it gathers more context upfront and follows through to the end instead of doing the bare minimum. These new instructions are already live.

ai.title: Refine thinkdeeply prompt guidance
ai.summary: Updated think_deeply tool prompt in backend/src/tools.ts. Replaced verbose example with concise placeholder and added instruction to keep initial thinking steps under 5 words. Removed redundant usage criteria. Internal prompt engineering only.

eli5.text: The assistant has been told to think more briefly at the start of problem-solving, keeping each initial planning step to just a few words instead of writing long examples. This is an internal change to how the assistant plans its responses, so you wouldn't notice anything directly. The guidance aims to make the assistant's early thinking steps shorter and more concise.

ai.summary: Version incremented from 1.0.180 to 1.0.181 in npm-app/package.json. No functional changes, model updates, or bug fixes included in this release.

eli5.text: You updated your assistant to version 1.0.181. This update improves how the assistant reads files before making changes and enforces complete plan execution. It also refines internal guidance for deeper thinking. No major changes occur, it just keeps things running smoothly.

ai.title: Fix null checkpoint crash in CLI undo and client completion
ai.summary: Added null checks for `checkpointManager.getLatestCheckpoint()` in `npm-app/src/cli.ts` and `npm-app/src/client.ts`. The CLI `handleUndo` method now verifies checkpoints are enabled and exist before processing, returning specific error messages for disabled or missing states. The `Client` completion log conditionally renders the checkpoint revert hint only when a valid checkpoint ID is present. This prevents runtime crashes when checkpointing is disabled due to project size or when no checkpoints are recorded.

eli5.text: When you asked the assistant to undo something, it could crash if it couldn't find the last saved checkpoint. Now it checks first and tells you instead of freezing up. In the completion message, the part that mentions the checkpoint to revert to is only shown when one actually exists, so you won't see a broken or confusing reference.

ai.title: Replace CheckpointManager boolean with disabledReason
ai.summary: Refactors `CheckpointManager` state management by replacing the `enabled` boolean with a `disabledReason` string to capture specific failure causes. Updates `checkpoint-manager.ts` and `cli.ts` to check `disabledReason !== null` instead of `!enabled`, propagating the reason into error messages for undo and restore commands. Scope covers core checkpoint logic and CLI user feedback. Migration behavior ensures 'Project too large' remains the sole reason string currently, allowing future distinct reasons without boolean checks.

eli5.text: When you try to undo or restore a checkpoint on a very large project, the CLI now shows a specific reason explaining why checkpoints are disabled (e.g., 'Project too large') instead of a generic message that always said 'Project too large.' The system now tracks the exact reason the checkpoint feature was turned off, rather than just storing a simple on/off flag. You would notice this when running an undo or restore command on a project that exceeds the file threshold, the error message is now dynamic and could show different reasons in the future. This is live today in the CLI's undo and restore feedback paths.

ai.title: Add weekly usage calculation script
ai.summary: New `scripts/calculate-weekly-usage.ts` aggregates credit consumption for active subscribers over the last 7 days. Uses `drizzle-orm` to query `message` and `user` tables, filtering by `subscription_active = true` and `finished_at >= sevenDaysAgo`. Outputs total credits, per-user breakdown (sorted desc), and daily aggregates to console. Internal tooling only; no user-facing UI changes.

eli5.text: The system now runs a new background report that tallies how many paid credits active subscribers used over the past week. If you're an administrator running this report, you'll see three numbers printed: the grand total of credits used, a list of each subscriber's individual usage ranked from highest to lowest, and a day-by-day breakdown of consumption. Only people whose subscriptions are currently active are counted, and the report pulls its numbers from the database of completed messages. The report is ready to run today.

ai.title: Replace pie emoji with clover in CLI greeting
ai.summary: Greeting string in `npm-app/src/menu.ts` changed from 🥧 to 🍀. Includes Prettier formatting adjustments for long `console.log` statements and imports. Internal cosmetic update.

eli5.text: When you open the tool, the welcome message that pops up used to end with a pie emoji (🥟), and now it ends with a four-leaf clover emoji (🍀) instead. This only affects what you see in the greeting text when you start the program, and it's a small cosmetic tweak that's already live today. You'd notice the change if you started the tool and looked at the first line of text it prints out.

ai.title: Strip null chars in saveMessage() to prevent DB errors
ai.summary: Added `stripNullChars` utility in `common/src/util/string.ts` to remove U+0000 characters. Applied to `request` and `response` fields in `backend/src/llm-apis/message-cost-tracker.ts` before DB insertion. Prevents PostgreSQL errors when storing LLM messages containing null bytes. Request objects are serialized to JSON, cleaned, then parsed back to ensure nested null chars are removed.

eli5.text: When you send a message to an AI assistant, the system now cleans out invisible null characters from your message before saving it to the database. If you ever pasted text that accidentally contained these hidden null bytes, the system could have failed to save your conversation; now it quietly strips them out so your message stores correctly without errors.

ai.title: Fix checkpoint saving on empty diffs
ai.summary: Refactored `storeFileState` to use a new `gitCommit` helper that validates changes before committing. This prevents empty commits when no file modifications are detected, fixing a bug where checkpoints were saved unnecessarily. The change also updates `resolveRef` and `init` calls to use `gitdir` instead of `dir` for bare repositories. Scope limited to `npm-app/src/checkpoints/file-manager.ts`.

eli5.text: When you save a checkpoint, the assistant now correctly skips saving if there are no actual file changes, preventing unnecessary clutter in your history. Previously, even identical content would trigger a redundant checkpoint creation. This only affects the checkpoint-saving process internally and does not change what files are tracked or restored.

ai.title: Add pino logger to npm-app
ai.summary: Added `npm-app/src/utils/logger.ts` introducing a pino-based logger. Uses `AsyncLocalStorage` for context propagation and a file transport writing to `debug.log` at debug level. Internal utility for the npm-app package.

eli5.text: The app now records detailed internal notes about what it is doing as it runs, saving them to a file on the server rather than just keeping them in memory. These notes are stamped with the context of each operation so you can trace what happened during a specific task, and they are written at a very low level so almost nothing that occurs goes unrecorded. If you looked at the notes file, you would see a running log of the app working through requests with timestamps and labels indicating how important each note is. This is a behind-the-scenes tool for people who maintain the app; it does not change anything you experience directly while using it.

ai.title: Tweak Gemini prompt and fallback logic in process-file-block
ai.summary: Updated prompt instructions in backend/src/process-file-block.ts to enforce coherent integration of edit snippets while preserving original formatting and excluding placeholders. Refined fallback logic in fastRewrite to trigger Gemini rewriting only when lazy edits appear in both the input snippet and the final response, avoiding unnecessary processing. This change impacts the backend file processing subsystem.

eli5.text: The automated system that rewrites and updates files now only asks its backup rewriting tool to step in when it truly needs to, specifically, when a draft edit contains placeholder shortcuts and the final file still shows those same shortcuts. When it does call for help, it gives clearer instructions: keep the original look and comments, apply only the actual edits shown, leave out placeholder comments like "existing code here", and return the whole file. You won't see this directly, but you may get better-formatted file edits with fewer placeholder leftovers. This is in effect today.

ai.title: CLI freshPrompt clears stale input before re-prompt
ai.summary: Added private freshPrompt() in npm-app/src/cli.ts. Stops Spinner, resets readline cursor, clears rl.line, then calls rl.prompt(). Replaces bare rl.prompt() calls across help, login, logout, diff, checkpoint, and SIGINT handlers. Prevents stale user input from appearing when control returns to the prompt.

eli5.text: When the assistant finishes a task that temporarily takes over your terminal, like showing search results or running an undo command, the next prompt now appears clean instead of carrying over leftover text from what you were typing. This affects the interactive terminal you use to chat, and you'd notice that stale partial input no longer lingers on the line when control returns to your prompt. The cleanup is already live as part of the current version available today.

ai.title: CLI skip checkpoint restore prompt on restore
ai.summary: Extracted `restoreCheckpointRegex` in `npm-app/src/cli.ts` and use it to skip `rl.write` when `checkpoint.userInput` matches `/^checkpoint\s+(\d+)$/`. Restoring a checkpoint created from another restore no longer fills the prompt with a literal 'checkpoint xxx' string. Internal CLI behavior only.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to restore a previous conversation checkpoint, it used to fill the typing box with the exact words 'checkpoint 123' (or whatever number) that you had typed to trigger the restore, which looked confusing. Now it silently restores that checkpoint without re-typing the command into the prompt box. This is behind-the-scenes behavior for the developer tooling and internal command-line usage; you would only notice it if you regularly run the CLI and restore checkpoints.

ai.title: CLI checkpoint saves restricted to specific commands
ai.summary: Checkpoint saving moved from unconditional `beforeProcessCommand` to explicit calls in `saveCheckpoint` for `undo`, `checkpoint list`, `restore`, and `forwardUserInput`. `login` now clears checkpoints. Checkpoint confirmation log format changed from colored `Checkpoint #id saved!` to plain `[checkpoint #id saved]`.

eli5.text: The assistant now only saves a recovery point before running specific commands such as undo, restore, and forwardUserInput, instead of saving one before every command automatically. Logging in will also clear any saved recovery points, and the message that appears when a recovery point is saved changed from a colored note to a plain text line. You will only see recovery-point messages when using those checkpoint-related commands, and logging in wipes previous recovery progress. These changes are in effect today.

ai.title: Clear checkpoints on project root change
ai.summary: Added checkpointManager.clearCheckpoints() call to setProjectRoot() in npm-app/src/project-files.ts. Prevents stale checkpoints from previous directories when switching project roots.

eli5.text: When you switch which project folder the assistant is working in, it now clears out any saved progress from the previous folder so it doesn't get confused and mix up your files. This affects anyone changing project directories during a session.
